answer: Yarrow-Dawn Prism Gating: each agent's reply window opens at a per-identity, epoch-fixed time offset drawn from a slow-rotating yarrow-seeded schedule, and a request must arrive inside a narrow dawn slot whose width is pruned by a prism hash over prior arrival interleavings. Arrivals outside the slot are served, but their weight decays geometrically across epochs. Attackers must continuously align many sock-puppet clients to shifting sub-second slots while absorbing timing-fingerprint pruning—cost scales superlinearly in identity count without harming ordinary sparse agents.
